title: Live imaging of microtubule dynamics at excitatory presynaptic boutons in primary hippocampal neurons and acute hippocampal slices
protocol: Prepare complete HBSS as recording medium and warm it up in a 37°C water bath.
Stabilize the temperature and humidity of incubator before imaging.
Select axons based on morphology (smaller diameter than dendrites and no spine structures along the neurite) and uniformly anterograde movement (toward the distal tip of the neurite) of EB3 comets.
Determine proximal axonal segments by locating the cell body and tracing the distance from the cell body based on real distance in μm in a still image taken with the camera.
Pre-treat neurons with 50 μM D-AP5 for 6–12 hours prior to live imaging in complete neurobasal medium.
Change the medium to complete HBSS supplemented with 50 μM D-AP5 before imaging.
Wash neurons three times with complete HBSS medium.
Add complete HBSS medium supplemented with 20 μM bicuculline or DMSO for neuronal activity induction.
Acquire movies at 1 frame/3–4 seconds, capturing 3 z-stacks at a step size of 0.4 μm for 3 minutes for dual channel acquisition.
Start movie acquisition 1 minute after inducing neuronal activity to ensure consistency and stabilization of temperature and CO2 flow.
Perform maximum intensity projections of movies using Image Math within Andor software.
Export Tiff files from the Andor software.
Analyze exported Tiff files in ImageJ.
Transfer acute slices onto millicell membrane upside down in MatTek dishes with 1 mL of warm fresh sterile medium.
Place the MatTek dish in a temperature-controlled chamber attached to the microscope.
Maintain temperature at 37°C and CO2 flow at 5% to promote cell viability and optical stability during live imaging.
Select electroporated hippocampal neurons from the CA1 region for imaging using an inverted Nikon Ti-E microscope operated by Nikon Elements Software.
Use 488 and 561 nm lasers as light sources, shuttered by Acousto-Optic Tunable Filters (AOTF).
Acquire live-imaging of EB3 comets relative to vGlut1 positive stable puncta within 50–100 μm of cell bodies for 300 s.
Use a 60× oil-immersion objective with NA1.4 during imaging.
Capture images at 1 frame every 3 seconds.
